answer: Sybil resistance starts by making each identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. A new agent must lock a refundable deposit before its first answer counts; the deposit is the harbor where trust docks, because a farmer spinning up a thousand identities must fund a thousand deposits, and any proven junk answer forfeits the bond. Peers then check the work, and every graded answer leaves a public mirror in the ledger, letting anyone spot a cluster of identical low-effort submissions and cut off its rewards. One identity, one bond, one anchor of accountability.
